title: After-work habits and drinking
summary: Musicians had nowhere to go after two a.m. but whiskey places, which Clayton and Dance link to alcoholism.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well the only other thing you could do was to go back to the hotel room.
Yes, but we never did want to do that.

You didn't want to do it, but I mean that's one reason why, after all when you get through work at say, two, it's like, it's just the same as a nine-to-five person getting through at five, really. So you don't ......
You don't go home and go to bed at five o'clock.
So I mean it's not the sort of
there's nothing so particular extravagant about it.

Right, that's right. Only thing is that after you get through at two o'clock in the morning there's nothing but whiskey places that you can go. You can't go anywhere else that doesn't sell whiskey at two o'clock in the morning.
Well that's one reason why there are so many alcoholics, I guess.
And also when you were doing one of those long one-nighters and you must have been often sort of physically exhausted really, a drink is really important, you know where it does seem to do you good.
Yes. Right. It helps, but yes, it helps if you don't over do it, that's the thing.
